{{etydate|second half of the 16th century|ref1={{R:Dictionary.com|for example|pos=''idiom''|noformat=yes||17 March 2026}}}}.

===Pronunciation===

* {{hyph|en|for ex|am|ple}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-for example.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Prepositional phrase===
{{en-prepphr}}

# {{senseid|en|as an example}} {{lb|en|conjunctive}} As an example.
#: {{syn|en|as<l:formal,somewhat,dated>|e.g.|for instance|like<l:informal>|such as}}
#: {{uxa|en|The book has quite a few plot holes. '''For example''', it's never explained why the main character came to town.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1981|author=w:William Irwin Thompson|title=The Time Falling Bodies Take to Light:Mythology, Sexuality and the Origins of Culture|page=12|text=For a structuralist like Edmund Leach, the structure ''is'' the meaning. Genesis, '''for example''', is about incest taboos; all the rest is noise and mystification.}}

====Usage notes====
* Often written with the Latin {{lg|initialism}} {{m|en|e.g.}} ({{m|la|exemplī grātiā}}), {{lg|rare|rarely}} with the initialism {{m|en|f.e.}}{{ref|{{cite-book|entry=f.e.|title=The Oxford Dictionary of Abbreviations|en-GB|year=1998|newversion=quoted in|title2=Encyclopedia.com|archiveurl2=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026181251/https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/fe|accessdate2=2026-03-17|url2=https://www.encyclopedia.com/humanities/dictionaries-thesauruses-pictures-and-press-releases/fe|archivedate=2021-10-26}}}} or {{m|en|f.ex.}}
